summary: Explains meta's free-form actions and details flush_handlers (runs notified handlers; inserted implicitly after pre/post tasks, roles, and tasks) and refresh_inventory (2.0; reloads inventory sources, keeps add_host and group_by hosts, can't refresh a script's own cache). Neither refresh_inventory nor add_host adds hosts to the current play, but delegate_to can reach new hosts.
questions: What actions can the meta module run?
How do I reload my dynamic inventory in the middle of a play?
Will refresh_inventory make new hosts part of the current play?
Does refresh_inventory keep hosts I added with add_host?
Why does refresh_inventory return stale data from my inventory script?
When does Ansible implicitly flush handlers?

answer_card.title: meta: flush_handlers and refresh_inventory
answer_card.answer_md:
`meta` takes a free-form action: `clear_facts`, `clear_host_errors`, `end_host`, `end_play`, `flush_handlers`, `noop`, `refresh_inventory`, `reset_connection`, `end_batch`, `end_role`.

- `flush_handlers`: runs handlers notified so far. Ansible inserts it implicitly after pre/post tasks, the final role execution, and the main tasks section.
- `refresh_inventory` (2.0): reloads inventory sources and host/group structure, preserving hosts from `add_host` and groups from `group_by`. Dynamic inventory scripts are re-executed; if a script uses its own cache, Ansible can't refresh it (disable the cache or use an inventory plugin, e.g. `amazon.aws.aws_ec2`).

Neither `refresh_inventory` nor `add_host` adds hosts to the hosts the **current** play iterates over, but you can `delegate_to` new hosts.
